subject: Post-demo compliance recap & subprocessor follow-ups (EmeraldTech)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@emeraldtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo compliance recap & subprocessor follow-ups (EmeraldTech)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. A quick recap and the handful of items we promised after the demo so your security and procurement teams can move quickly: 

1) SOC 2 status: you mentioned EmeraldTech recently started a SOC 2 Type II assessment. Can you confirm the expected completion month and whether you can share the SOC 2 Type II report or an interim SOC 2 readiness report once available?

2) Subprocessors / cloud providers: please send the full list of third-party processors that will touch customer data (we typically see AWS, GCP, third-party logging or analytics tools). If you have a CSV or procurement roster, that would be ideal.

3) Data scope & residency: we need to confirm which data classes will be sent to Redwood (PII, user-generated content, PHI if applicable) and preferred residency (US / EU). We can provide a short mapping template.

4) Vendor security questionnaire: to speed evaluation, I attached our vendor security questionnaire PDF and shared our short subprocessor mapping template. If you prefer, we can host a synchronous security call — Marissa (cc'd) can join for technical compliance details and Ben can join for an architecture deep-dive.

Next steps I'd propose:
- Emily: share current SOC 2 status + estimated report date and the subprocessor roster (CSV preferred) by EOD Wed Oct 21
- Connor / Marissa / Ben: schedule a 30-min security follow-up (options below)

Proposed times (PST): Wed 10/21 9:00–9:30am, 11:30–12:00pm, Thu 10/22 8:30–9:00am — let me know what works for your team.

Attachments: redwood-demo-deck.pdf, redwood-security-questionnaire.pdf, subprocessor-mapping-template.csv

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Park <emily.park@emeraldtech.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo compliance recap & subprocessor follow-ups (EmeraldTech)

Connor —

Appreciate the clear recap and the materials. Quick status from our side after internal sync: 

- SOC 2: our audit window began in Aug; auditors expect to issue Type II reports by early December 2026. We can share an interim control matrix and our SOC 2 Type I artifacts this week.

- Subprocessors: attached is a preliminary roster (EmeraldTech_Vendor_SQ.xlsx). High-level: primary infra is AWS (us-east-1) for production, GCP for analytics, and a third-party logging vendor (LogStream). We will pull a CSV export for you by EOD Wed.

- Data scope: current integration would send account-level metadata and user messages (no PHI for this use case). We may route limited PII (email, name). We will confirm exact fields in the CSV.

- Questionnaire: will route the questionnaire to our Security team; Paul (cc'd) is leading procurement and will coordinate required signatures/PO.

We can do Thu 10/22 8:30–9:00am PST for the security follow-up; Marissa and Ben joining is perfect.

Attaching: EmeraldTech_Vendor_SQ.xlsx (roster snapshot).

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of Product Ops | EmeraldTech
emily.park@emeraldtech.com | +1 (206) 555-3344

Hi Emily / Paul / Security team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the roster snapshot. Forwarding our questionnaire and a short mapping template to make the review easier. Key asks for your security team before our call: 

- Please attach SOC 2 Type I artifacts or interim control evidence if available (controls matrix, auditor name)
- CSV export of subprocessor roster with columns: vendor_name, purpose, data_types_processed, region, contact_email

Connor / Ben —

I reviewed the roster snapshot Emily sent. Next steps for us ahead of the Thu call: 

1) I'll run a quick baseline check against our accepted subprocessor patterns (AWS, GCP, common logging vendors) and flag anything unusual.
2) Ben — please prepare a 5-slide data-flow slide showing how Redwood will handle kv-cache, prefix caching, and where logs or telemetry may touch third-party services. That will help answer their procurement questions live.
